TABATABAI:2:164-165/r1.claim: Cloud is condensed vapor that yields rain; vapor near the ground is called fog, and higher vapor is cloud or related terms. Its movement and rainfall are subdued by wind, cold, and other forces by God’s permission.

TABATABAI:2:164-165/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:164-165/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:164-165/r2.claim: The night–day cycle, rain, wind, and clouds are the general processes composing the terrestrial order; this verse details in one respect the provision described in another verse.

TABATABAI:2:164-165/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:164-165/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:164-165/r3.claim: Aql means complete understanding; as a faculty of discernment it is the perceiving human self, not a subsidiary power like sight or memory.

TABATABAI:2:164-165/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:164-165/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:164-165/r4.claim: Wind’s existence points to God; its integration with other things points to one God for the world, and its role in human life points to the same God for humans and the rest of creation.

TABATABAI:2:164/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:164/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:164/r1.claim: The changing cosmos maintains one connected, ordered system: both its assembled whole and its smallest parts display continuous governance, though each entity differs in nature and properties; this points to one creator and governor (his second proof).

TABATABAI:2:164/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:164/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:164/r2.claim: Earth-dwelling humans depend for material life on the connected cosmic order, including celestial light and heat, day and night, wind, clouds, and rain; their creator and governor is therefore the same God (his third proof).

TABATABAI:2:164/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:164/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:164/r3.claim: The same God grants what creatures need for present and final happiness: the afterlife follows this world, so its governor must be the governor of this life; this establishes the names al-Raḥmān and al-Raḥīm.

TABATABAI:2:164/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:164/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:164/r4.claim: The opening inna signals that verse 164 explains and establishes the preceding verse.

ASAD-NOTES:2:163#n130/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:163#n130/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:163#n130/r1.claim: The verse invites rational reflection on nature's daily wonders, including human ingenuity in shipbuilding, as signs of a conscious creative Power pervading the universe.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:164/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:164/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:164/r1.claim: The verse follows a declaration of God's oneness and mercy with eight cosmological proofs for those claims.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:164/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:164/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:164/r10.claim: Learning natural sciences enables careful observation and discovery of divine laws and signs; the Qur'an leads people through knowledge and science to faith and guidance.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:164/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:164/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:164/r2.claim: The signs are ordinary natural events surrounding people, so humanity lives amid daily evidence of God's existence, unity, and power.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:164/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:164/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:164/r3.claim: Nature itself is miraculous, but familiarity makes people miss its signs; a differently formed cosmos or earth would not support known life.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:164/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:164/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:164/r4.claim: The regular alternation of night and day benefits all living things, especially plants.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:164/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:164/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:164/r5.claim: Ships at sea exemplify how transport and the divine laws enabling its use sustain and ease human life.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:164/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:164/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:164/r6.claim: Rain makes the world habitable, while winds and clouds support meteorological order, plant fertilization, and rainfall distribution.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:164/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:164/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:164/r7.claim: Nature and its continuing order depend on God and prove divine unity, uniqueness, knowledge, will, power, and ongoing control; without that relation the universe would vanish or become chaos.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:164/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:164/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:164/r8.claim: Both revelation and the universe contain signs of God, but only people who use reason can recognize them; reason must be exercised well.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:164/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:164/r9.speaker: Fahreddin er-Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:164/r9.claim: Al-Razi says the verse requires rational proofs, rather than reliance on transmitted knowledge alone, to establish the Creator's existence.

QIRAAT-ER:2:164:44#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:164:44#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:164:44#1/r1.claim: The singular reading may denote one atmospheric force or carry a punitive connotation, shifting the sign from gentle plurality to singular power.

STUDYQURAN:2:164/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:164/r1.speaker: Some
STUDYQURAN:2:164/r1.claim: Some commentators connect the verse to idolaters demanding a sign, including turning Ṣafā into gold or asking how one God can encompass all people.

STUDYQURAN:2:164/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:164/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:164/r10.claim: Clouds course between earth and sky under divine subjection, like other things described as subjected to God or made useful to people.

STUDYQURAN:2:164/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:164/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:164/r2.claim: The Quran repeatedly presents natural and cosmic phenomena as divine signs, sometimes singly and sometimes in a series.

STUDYQURAN:2:164/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:164/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:164/r3.claim: The variation of night and day is cited as a sign elsewhere in the Quran.

STUDYQURAN:2:164/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:164/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:164/r4.claim: The creation of the heavens and earth is cited as a sign elsewhere in the Quran.

STUDYQURAN:2:164/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:164/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:164/r5.claim: The Quran also mentions ships sailing at sea in several other passages.

STUDYQURAN:2:164/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:164/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:164/r6.claim: Ships are the verse’s sole human-made items, yet depend closely on nature and remain fragile against the sea, making seafaring itself a reminder of God.

STUDYQURAN:2:164/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:164/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:164/r7.claim: Other passages depict people turning sincerely to God during sea storms and lapsing after danger passes.

STUDYQURAN:2:164/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:164/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:164/r8.claim: The revival of the earth after its death is another Quranic sign repeated in several passages.

STUDYQURAN:2:164/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:164/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:164/r9.claim: Winds are signs and blessings, and the word rīḥ is root-related to rūḥ, or spirit.
